pr.body:
All these functions end up calling `visit_f64` so rewriting these functions to avoid dependence on the visitor type `V` is a no-brainer:

  - `parse_long_integer`
  - `parse_decimal`
  - `parse_exponent`
  - `parse_exponent_overflow`
  - `visit_f64_from_parts`

Slightly alleviates #313.

---

Benchmarks on the [minimal Pandoc example](https://github.com/serde-rs/json/issues/313#issuecomment-298806623) show a 10% reduction in both build time and memory usage:

- 14.4 s → 13.0 s
- 451 M → 407 M

Thanks! 23% compile time improvement from this is impressive and there is a lot more we can do to improve it further. We definitely need to evaluate the runtime performance impact too though. I don't have time this week to put into benchmarking but I expect to get to it this weekend.

Benchmark results are in! The first two commits show no performance regression and a consistent 15% improvement in compile time on the [json-benchmark](https://github.com/serde-rs/json-benchmark) repo. The third commit runs about 30% slower across the board and confusingly also compiles 20-30% slower for me than the other commits. So I am merging 476e753db863c7f9059f82c5ae8c6a2220b2fc5c and 2b68532e9d3ad68df07c3b4cf221dc9dbaa40f6e but not 7b9ad82c9562e2805ff40d406b1998ae69200f14. We will need to figure out what went wrong there. Possibly a missing `#[inline]` on one of the functions.
